revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Flooring
revealWordProblem.text:
A garden designer wants to cover a gazebo floor with tiles. The gazebo floor is a regular decagon with equal sides, shown here with a side of 3¾ feet and a distance of 5¾ feet from the center to the middle of a side.
Question: If floor tiles cost $2.89 per square foot, what budget do you recommend the designer have for the tiles?
revealWordProblem.imageAlt: A regular decagon gazebo floor labeled 3 and three-fourths feet on one side and 5 and three-fourths feet from the center to the middle of a side.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Decompose the decagon into 10 identical triangles that meet at the center. Each triangle has a base of 3¾ = 3.75 feet and a height of 5¾ = 5.75 feet, so its area is ½ × 3.75 × 5.75 = 10.78125 square feet. Ten triangles give 107.8125 square feet. At $2.89 per square foot, the tile cost is 107.8125 × 2.89 ≈ $311.58. I would recommend a budget of about $320 so there is room for a few extra tiles for cuts and breakage.

questions.stem: An L-shaped room is made of two rectangles: 10 ft × 6 ft and 4 ft × 3 ft. What is the total area?
questions.explanation: Area 1 = 10 × 6 = 60 sq ft. Area 2 = 4 × 3 = 12 sq ft. Total = 60 + 12 = 72 sq ft.
hints: The L-shape is already split into two rectangles for you: 10 × 6 and 4 × 3.
Find each rectangle's area separately with A = l × w, then combine — joined shapes mean adding.
Compute 10 × 6 and 4 × 3, then add the two results. Label your answer in sq ft.
questions.stemEs: Una habitación en forma de L está formada por dos rectángulos: 10 ft × 6 ft y 4 ft × 3 ft. ¿Cuál es el área total?
questions.explanationEs: Área 1 = 10 × 6 = 60 sq ft. Área 2 = 4 × 3 = 12 sq ft. Total = 60 + 12 = 72 sq ft.
hintsEs: La figura en L ya está dividida en dos rectángulos por ti: 10 × 6 y 4 × 3.
Halla el área de cada rectángulo por separado con A = l × a y luego combínalas: figuras unidas significan sumar.
Calcula 10 × 6 y 4 × 3, y luego suma los dos resultados. Etiqueta tu respuesta en pies².

questions.stem: A rectangular patio is 15 ft × 10 ft with a 5 ft × 4 ft rectangular flower bed cut out. What is the remaining area?
questions.explanation: Patio = 15 × 10 = 150 sq ft. Cutout = 5 × 4 = 20 sq ft. Remaining = 150 − 20 = 130 sq ft.
choiceFeedback: A thin rectangle and a square can differ.
hints: The flower bed is CUT OUT of the patio — that phrase tells you which operation to use.
Find the full patio area (15 × 10) and the cutout area (5 × 4), then remove the cutout.
Compute 15 × 10 and 5 × 4, then subtract the flower bed's area from the patio's area.
questions.stemEs: Un patio rectangular mide 15 ft × 10 ft y tiene recortado un jardín rectangular de 5 ft × 4 ft. ¿Cuál es el área restante?
questions.explanationEs: Patio = 15 × 10 = 150 sq ft. Recorte = 5 × 4 = 20 sq ft. Área restante = 150 − 20 = 130 sq ft.
hintsEs: El jardín está RECORTADO del patio: esa frase te dice qué operación usar.
Halla el área total del patio (15 × 10) y el área del recorte (5 × 4), y luego quita el recorte.
Calcula 15 × 10 y 5 × 4, y luego resta el área del jardín del área del patio.

reviewHighlights.watchOut: A common mistake in Area of Composite Figures is adding every piece even when a piece has been cut out of the figure. For a 10 ft by 8 ft rectangle with a 3 ft by 2 ft rectangular notch cut from one corner, students compute the full rectangle 10 × 8 = 80 sq ft and stop, or they add the notch instead of removing it (80 + 6 = 86 sq ft) instead of subtracting it: 80 − (3 × 2) = 80 − 6 = 74 sq ft. Before submitting, check whether each piece is part of the figure (add it) or missing from the figure (subtract it).

level1.stem: When should you subtract areas instead of adding them to find the area of a composite figure?
choices: When one shape is larger than the other
When a piece is cut out or removed from a larger shape
level1.explanation: Subtract when a piece is removed from a larger shape (like a window cut from a wall). Add when two shapes are joined together (like an L-shape).
choiceFeedback: Overlap is different — subtracting is for a piece removed.
Size alone doesn't decide — subtract only when part is removed.
Not always — you add pieces that are joined together.
hints: Think of real examples: a window in a wall versus two rooms joined into an L-shape.
Ask for each choice: is material missing from the shape, or are pieces being combined?
Picture a wall with a window: you can't paint the glass, so its area comes OFF the wall's area. Match that idea to a choice.
level1.stemEs: ¿Cuándo debes restar áreas en lugar de sumarlas para hallar el área de una figura compuesta?
level1.explanationEs: Resta cuando se quita una pieza de una figura más grande (como una ventana recortada en una pared). Suma cuando dos figuras se unen (como una figura en forma de L).
choicesEs: Cuando una figura es más grande que la otra
Siempre se resta — nunca se suma
Cuando se corta o se quita una parte de una figura más grande
hintsEs: Piensa en ejemplos reales: una ventana en una pared frente a dos cuartos unidos en forma de L.
Pregunta en cada opción: ¿le falta material a la figura o se están combinando piezas?
Imagina una pared con una ventana: no puedes pintar el vidrio, así que su área se QUITA del área de la pared. Une esa idea con una opción.

level3.prompt: A T-shaped room can be decomposed in two different ways. Show both ways and prove they give the same total area. Use a T-shape where the top is 14 ft × 4 ft and the stem is 6 ft × 10 ft.
level3.sentenceFrame: Way 1: I split it into ___ and ___. Areas: ___ + ___ = ___. Way 2: I used a ___ rectangle and subtracted ___. Areas: ___ − ___ = ___. Both give ___ sq ft.
level3.hint: Write original area formula and scaled formula; compare.
hints: The T's top slab is 14 × 4 and its stem is 6 × 10. Way 1 simply adds those two rectangles.
For Way 2, wrap the whole T in one big rectangle and subtract the empty corner rectangles.
Way 1: 14 × 4 plus 6 × 10. Then build the big rectangle for Way 2 and show the subtraction lands on the same total.
level3.explanation: Way 1 splits the T into its two named rectangles: 14 × 4 = 56 plus 6 × 10 = 60, a total of 116 sq ft. Way 2 wraps the T in a 14 ft × 14 ft rectangle worth 196 sq ft and subtracts the two empty 4 ft × 10 ft corners, 196 − 80 = 116 sq ft — the same region is being measured, so the decomposition you choose cannot change the area.
level3.explanationEs: La Manera 1 divide la T en sus dos rectángulos nombrados: 14 × 4 = 56 más 6 × 10 = 60, un total de 116 sq ft. La Manera 2 envuelve la T en un rectángulo de 14 ft × 14 ft que vale 196 sq ft y resta las dos esquinas vacías de 4 ft × 10 ft, 196 − 80 = 116 sq ft: se está midiendo la misma región, así que la forma en que la descompongas no puede cambiar el área.
level3.promptEs: Un cuarto en forma de T se puede descomponer de dos maneras diferentes. Muestra las dos maneras y demuestra que dan la misma área total. Usa una forma de T donde la parte de arriba mida 14 pies × 4 pies y el tronco mida 6 pies × 10 pies.
hintsEs: La parte de arriba de la T es 14 × 4 y su tallo es 6 × 10. La Vía 1 simplemente suma esos dos rectángulos.
Para la Vía 2, envuelve toda la T en un rectángulo grande y resta los rectángulos vacíos de las esquinas.
Vía 1: 14 × 4 más 6 × 10. Luego arma el rectángulo grande de la Vía 2 y muestra que la resta llega al mismo total.
